exercise.title: A whole key in one place
exercise.why: Every chord of a key has a shape inside any five frets of the neck, so you can change chord by changing shape and leave your hand where it is.

cells.text:
The panels below show the 1, 4 and 5 chords of G major where they meet on the neck: G in the E shape, C in the A shape and D in the C shape. Play each chord, and check that your hand stays over the same frets.
Go round G, C, D and back to G until each change is a new shape and not a move along the neck.

Press a chord in the Chords row below to ring its notes in the position and hear it. These are the three minor chords of G major, as three-note shapes on the G, B and high e strings in the same area.
Play each one straight after the G chord, until you can find all three without pressing the row.

Press Play below to start the metronome, and strum the chord in the lit box, every one inside the same area of the neck.
If a chord sends your hand up the neck, stop and find its shape in the area before you go on.
